title: Stream Cushion Admission and Attention Pathway Optimizer
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement: Persistent tail latency spikes for mixed-size workloads during continuous batching. Short interactive requests (<=64 tokens) are frequently delayed behind large prefill-heavy requests, and the serving runtime occasionally chooses attention kernels that amplify memory pressure on A100 and RTX-class machines, worsening 95/99 latency.

Goal: Implement a combined admission + kernel-routing feature that reduces tail latencies without sacrificing throughput: (1) a low-overhead "stream cushion" admission window that proactively reserves micro-slots for short requests and prevents long prefill floods, and (2) an attention pathway optimizer that picks fused/unfused or tiled attention kernels per-batch based on a short runtime profile and KV-cache hit signals.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Reservation size: reserving a fixed percentage (3-5%) of slots ensures short requests see bounded waiting time but reduces peak throughput; we chose a dynamic cushion that scales with observed short-request proportion to minimize throughput loss.
- Kernel selection heuristic: we evaluated purely latency-based selection (choose fastest kernel historically) vs cost-aware selection (latency + GPU memory pressure). We adopted a hybrid score: estimated kernel exec time + alpha * memory_pressure_penalty (alpha tuned in experiments).
- Prefill gating: two strategies were prototyped: (A) strict prefill quanta that throttle prefill admission when short-request queue depth exceeds threshold, (B) interleaved prefill where prefill decode tasks yield periodically to short decode tasks. We selected B because it produced lower 99p latency in mixed synthetic + production traces.

Implementation plan:
1) Admission service: add a lightweight per-GPU cushion manager which maintains a short-window EWMA of short-request fraction, computes cushion_slots, and exposes a fast admission check used by the prefill scheduler.
2) Kernel profiler: add micro-benchmarks that run at startup and during low-load windows to update kernel cost table by (sequence_length, batch_size, kv_hit_rate) buckets.
3) Attention pathway optimizer: a scoring function that combines kernel cost table, current batch shape histogram, and memory pressure metric to pick kernel path before allocation. Fallback to stable kernel on unknown shapes.
4) Prefill scheduler: interleaved decode loop that yields after N tokens or M ms (configurable). Integrate with cushion manager to admit/hold prefill tasks.
5) Metrics & observability: track per-request queuing time, admission decisions, chosen kernel, kernel durations, memory pressure, and end-to-end latency percentiles in a new Grafana dashboard and alert rule for 99p regressions.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- 99p latency for short requests (<=64 tokens) decreases by >=30% under mixed workload synthetic test (50% short, 50% long prefill) compared to baseline.
- Total throughput loss <= 8% for the same mixed test.
- No regression in model quality or decoding correctness.
- Safe fallback path validated on canary region with zero customer errors for 24h.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for admission logic and kernel-scoring function.
- Cluster-integration test using hybrid trace generator (see tool in /tools/trace-gen) to replay production mixes with KV-hit variability.
- Canary rollout: start on runtime-canary-2 (non-critical customers) at 5% traffic, monitor metrics for 2h, then 25%, then 100% in that region if green.

Risks and mitigation:
- Kernel perf variance across GPU families: mitigate with continuous microbenchmarks and conservative memory_penalty factor. If variance is high, default to single stable kernel for that GPU family.
- Coordination latency: cushion manager must be extremely low overhead. Implement as per-GPU lock-free counters and avoid RPC for admission checks in hot path.
- Mis-tuned parameters causing throughput regression: run automated parameter sweep in staging and add an automatic rollback if throughput drops >10%.
